scope: Second and final bounded native-family actual six-HUD static sample: shown upper/lower/left covers, real lower90wu/upper40wu step connections, central bay and retired-strip window; two actual formal Plains controls.
reason: Visible nonuniform branch hierarchy, legible pale needles and genuinely bent roots on the real step edge resolve the first native sample antler-fence and internal-L-bracket failures sufficiently for this limited static covering sample.

observations.evidence: map1_thorn_hollow.png x190..849 y329..371 and y508..550; map2_thorn_elbow.png horizontal runs
observations.actual: Long narrow stem with short pale needles now alternates with sparse taller growth. Comparable antler forks no longer occupy every short module. The bottom run shows quiet spans and unequal branch lengths; the upper run is a continuous thin thorned vine rather than repeated equally heavy crowns. Wood light/shadow clusters remain clear.
observations.residual: Repeated source shapes remain discoverable and the horizontal habitat still follows a straight platform; this is a stylized local surface sample, not unique growth everywhere.

observations.type: Actual HUD observation plus source audit
observations.actual: The lower brown root leaves the upper run, bends along the actual exposed right lip in an uneven S contour, then joins the lower run. It no longer stands as a long straight post inside the wall. The upper40wu step is joined by a short bent root following its real edge. No obvious daylight gap or detached bracket remains at shown joins. Brown bare connection stays distinct from pale harmful spikes.
observations.source_limit: Independent alpha calculation finds all690/263 opaque native elbow pixels within corresponding real solid union. This does not establish physics or runtime hit fairness.

observations.evidence: Both Plains controls plus all4 Forest originals
observations.actual: Both regions retain the same courier, dark quiet terrain interior, small native clusters and broken green moss rim. Added warm wood and pale thorns provide Forest identity without replacing the shared terrain family. Short mouth down/left covers remain attached to actual edges, without detached hazard bricks.

observations.evidence: map1_thorn_hollow.png center x503..657/y504..550; map2_thorn_elbow.png center gap; map1_thorn_retired.png
observations.actual: The thin green central platform and open space remain visually identifiable, with no pale thorns introduced across the shown blunt root connection. Retired prototype window still contains no former floating horizontal thorn strip. Actor and HUD are visible in these staged poses.
observations.limit: Staged actor poses do not prove safe landings, collisions, resource fairness, movement occlusion or damage contact.
